correctness.rationale: For ordered alphabets of cardinality k>=3 and every integer 31<=n<=64, the classical factor-two inequality r(BWT(w))<=2 r(w) for the Lyndon primitive representative gives r_cyclic(w)>=ceil(n/2), since its endpoints differ. The proposed upper bound is not inferred from a search: witnesses.tsv contains exactly one ternary last-column word of each of the 34 lengths. Independently constructed the stable LF first-column permutation, verified it is an n-cycle, inverted it into a primitive input, explicitly sorted all n cyclic rotations to reproduce the last column, checked every linear adjacent last-column pair differs and counted exactly ceil(n/2) cyclic source transitions. Every 34 independent checks passed; third-symbol counts are exactly 14 with 2 occurrences, 16 with 4, 4 with 6, each a perturbation of binary alternating. This verifies the finite certificates and their all-alphabet extension without confusing existence at 34 lengths with a proof at all lengths.
residual_risks: Proof depends on the cited factor-two run theorem and standard BWT single-cycle criterion; one finite witness is an existence proof for each fixed integer length, not an exhaustive classification of optimal words.
